title: Marching order, stride and Sousa marches
summary: Parade lineup of large instruments in front and drums behind, four abreast, with a longer stride; marches like High Society and Panama.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Four sisters. Yes. All of them are the daughters. Great, man. I was going to ask about the marches. Do you remember how you would line up who was in front and who was in back in the arms? Yes, I do remember that.
Well, we all lined up the larger instruments. For instance, the bass, baritone, two trombones. The rest of four, you know, and then the alto players and the trumpets and the drums in the back.
The drums are always in back then. Right. They do that in New Orleans. Yes. I suppose it's a standard over there. And always four abreast then. That's right.
Did they march as fast then? The Army and high school bands all march so fast that they almost run.

We had a different step, you understand, than what the U is now. We had a longer stride than what... You have to swing. Yes. That's right. Longer stride. Now they use a little short. I don't know what you might call that... That's right.
Yeah, they used to go swinging down the street, but they do not do hard. Did they usually play a little bit slower, the marches, than they do today, you think? No, I think they're about the same.

Just about the same. They're all different. It was the steps, you understand, that they make now. They make short steps. We had a longer stride with us. Do you remember any of the other marches? You mentioned Sousa marches. Did they ever play High Society? High Society?
That was my favorite. Panama. Panama. Panama. Panama.
I think that was one we played. We played that. So many other heavy marches, you know.

Very good. Pretty good on that. You take your head, clarinet pots, cue it in. We take that up with the trumpet. With the trumpet? With the trumpet. With the trumpet. We did all of that. Last night you began to tell us a little bit about the dance arrangement when you play for dances.
